subject: Private deploy DPA: BYOK, operator access, and subprocessors

Subject: Private deployment DPA questions (BYOK + operator access)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the call this morning. As we start our procurement review for the on-prem/VPC deployment, Legal and Security at HelioHealth asked for a short write-up on the following items so they can approve the DPA addendum and BYOK approach: 

- Confirmation that customer-managed keys (BYOK) remain under our control and that Redwood cannot decrypt customer data without a documented breakglass or escrow event.
- Exact scope of Redwood operator access (if any) to the environment, logs, or telemetry, and whether operators could access unredacted customer prompts.
- Subprocessor list for the private deploy package (hosting partners, monitoring vendors) and notification windows for adding a new subprocessor.
- Data egress controls and cross-border transfer assurances for backups or audit artifacts.

Can you send a short, table-style summary and the suggested DPA language? We attached our initial questions (Helio_Questions_v1.xlsx).

We also copied Olive Bridge (security reviewer) to triage technical follow-ups.

Thanks,
Samir Patel

HelioHealth

Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA questions (BYOK + operator access)

Samir —

Appreciate the clear list. Summary below and attached is a short BYOK & DPA appendix that maps to each ask (Redwood_DPA_Byok_Appendix.pdf). High level: private deployments are designed so HelioHealth keeps cryptographic control, and Redwood operator access is strictly scoped and logged. Details: 

1) BYOK ownership & decryption
- Customer-held keys: keys are generated and stored in customer KMS/HSM. Redwood never has persistent key material.
- Breakglass / escrow: Redwood will only perform key decryption actions under a pre-agreed escrow procedure or court order. Any breakglass access requires a documented request, two-person operator approval, time-limited JIT token, and full-forensic logging.

2) Operator scope
- Routine operations: Redwood operators may perform platform-level diagnostics but only against metadata and redactable telemetry.
- No access to plaintext customer prompts, PII, or model inputs/outputs unless explicit, logged, and approved via breakglass.
- All operator sessions in private deployments are session-recorded and retained for 12 months by default (configurable).

3) Subprocessors
- Private deploy uses a short explicit subprocessor list limited to: Redwood Ops (on-call), Monitoring vendor (SentryCloud), and Cloud partner for hardware procurement (EdgeLabs) — full names/addresses in the appendix.
- Notification: 60-day notice for new subprocessors; emergency exceptions limited to critical security patches with post-notification and right-to-terminate clause.

4) Data egress & transfers
- Backups/audit artifacts: backups are encrypted with customer CMK before leaving the VPC. Transfer only occurs to customer-designated regions.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood will not move unencrypted data across geographies without written consent.

Next steps: if this aligns, propose a 30-min signatures call with Legal to walk the DPA appendix and implement two small edits your counsel may request.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick inline notes: 

- Breakglass wording: propose adding a step that requires a signed authorization token from customer Legal + a timestamped change ticket. JIT tokens should be single-use, expire in 4 hours, and require 2 operator approvals for any decryption. Retention: 24 months for session recordings is safer for audit; provide a configurable default of 12 months in the contract with option to extend.

- Operator scope: make explicit that operators only receive redacted logs by default; unredacted access requires a separate Technical Access Request (TAR) linked to the breakglass. Add requirement that TARs include incident ticket ID and a minimal data access justification.

- Subprocessors: the 60-day notice is fine; add a right-to-audit clause limited to attestation (no on-site audits). Also add a rollback clause for customers to terminate if a subprocessor materially changes services within 30 days of notification.

I attached a short operator runbook draft with the proposed mechanics and required customer approvals.

Irene Choi
Principal Security Engineer, Privacy Controls
Redwood Inference
